text:
devon: Heads-up — we started seeing a regression in comm/compute overlap after the graph-scheduler change landed (PR #4321). Latency p50 for multi-GPU TP=2/PP=1 went from 140ms -> 220ms on A100. Anyone else seeing this?

maya: saw the alert, digging. appears to correlate with the graph capture path switching to 'capture_per_batch' mode. :thinking_face:

sam: repro command I used: `./tools/bench --model gpt-small --tp 2 --pp 1 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --use-graphs` on the 8xA100 testbed. run id: run-20260312-09.

ryan: nvprof / nsight shows large stalls around all-reduce start. timeline snapshot: compute stream continues, cudaGraphLaunch returns early, but nccl op waits for a host-side sync (seen as SM stalls).

devon: exact symptom I saw — graph capture didn't record events on the comm stream, so replay schedule launches compute kernels before the host posts the event. That yields a serialized fallback where NCCL issues host syncs.

infra-bot: deploy:graph-scheduler v0.3.7 rolled 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC by zhang (sha: c3d9a7f).

zhang: looking at the PR diffs now. We moved to capture graphs once per batch to reduce capture overhead, but I see code removed the explicit `cudaEventRecord` between compute and comm streams in the capture path.

nina: repro profile attached (condensed):
```
Timeline (ms):
0.0  kernel FWD layer0 (compute_stream)
1.2  kernel FWD layer1 (compute_stream)
2.8  cudaGraphLaunch (compute_stream)
3.0  ncclAllReduce start (comm_stream)  <-- waits on host
3.0  SM stall due to host sync  (20ms)
23.0 ncclAllReduce resume
26.5 kernel BWD layer2 (compute_stream)
```

maya: I ran a simple isolated repro that toggles `record_event_between_streams` and the regression disappears when the event is present. So the problem is definitely missing stream synchronization inside the captured graph.

sam: odd: historically, graphs should be able to capture inter-stream dependencies if events are recorded during capture. Maybe the capture code path isn't creating events on the comm_stream (or using the wrong stream handle) when capture is enabled.

zhang: confirmed: in `graph_scheduler.cpp` we replaced `cudaEventCreateWithFlags(&e, cudaEventDisableTiming)` with `cudaEvent_t e; /* omitted */` and relied on stream semantics. That was to micro-optimize event allocs but broke cross-stream capture semantics.

devon: proposed temporary mitigation: add an opt-in flag `--disable-graph-capture` for Dedicated nodes while we patch, or re-enable event recording inside capture until we ensure the allocator handles events cheaply.

ryan: suggestion for fix that avoids perf regressions: reuse a preallocated pool of events (one per pair of streams) and still record them during capture. That keeps allocation overhead amortized. Also make sure we use `cudaEventDisableTiming` and `cudaEventRecord(e, comm_stream)` during capture so that the captured graph includes the dependency.

nina: test matrix notes: reproduced on CUDA 12.1 + NCCL 2.19, A100, driver 535.54.03. Single-node multi-GPU only. TP/PP configs with pipeline parallelism exhibit worse effect because compute and comm interleave tightly.

maya: I pushed a quick experiment branch zhang/graph-event-pool that reintroduces event recording but uses a lock-free pool. Bench results (same bench): p50 -> back to 145ms, p95 improved too. Will push PR for code review.

sam: also found a micro-optimization we can do: place the `cudaEventRecord` calls after the last kernel launch in capture so we don't insert extra host pauses. That way the graph captures a single dependency per batch.

devon: long-term we should add a unit test that captures a tiny graph with cross-stream events and asserts no host syncs on replay. Reproducer idea: minimal C repro that does `cudaGraphCaptureBegin`, launches kernels on stream0, records event to stream1, launches nccl op on stream1, `cudaGraphCaptureEnd`, then `cudaGraphLaunch` and nsight timeline dump.

ryan: assigning: zhang -> add pooled events + record during capture, maya -> add test case and bench harness update, devon -> coordinate QA nightly run.

zhang: ack. PR will include microbench and careful release notes: "Fix: restore cross-stream event recording during graph capture to preserve comm/compute dependencies; add pooled event allocator to avoid alloc overhead."

nina: nice catch. Also flagging for eng-sre: rolling patch needs canary on Dedicated clusters before wide roll. If canary fails, rollback path should be simple (flip feature flag).

sam: one more nuance: when using kernel selection heuristics that change kernel timings, the event placement may shift critical edges — adding tests that fuzz kernel sizes/seqlen is important.

devon: agreed. We should include fuzz cases: seq=512/1024/2048, batch=1/4/8, tp/pp permutations. I'll add that to the bench matrix.

maya: thanks all. I'll coordinate canary tomorrow and post results here. :eyes:
